You think popping a pimple pushes everything OUT. But watch what actually happens underneath your skin. Imagine we could shrink down and travel beneath the surface. Inside the skin is a tiny hair follicle clogged with sticky oil and dead skin cells, forming a swollen pimple above it. Now two fingers squeeze the pimple from both sides. Look underneath. The pressure crushes the clogged follicle from both directions. Some of the trapped material is forced upward through the opening and bursts out onto the surface. But that's only the part you can see. Deeper underneath, that same pressure can force material further into the surrounding tissue. Now your immune system reacts. Blood vessels expand. The surrounding tissue becomes red, swollen and inflamed. What looked like an empty pimple from the outside can actually be more irritated underneath. And repeatedly squeezing and damaging that tissue can increase your chance of infection and permanent acne scarring. So next time you see that satisfying POP… remember: you're watching what came OUT. You can't see what you may have pushed IN.
